evals.prompt: I keep missing it when Claude finishes a task while I'm away from my desk. Set up notifications to my phone.
evals.expected_output: The skill explains that Pushover needs two separate credentials (application token starting with 'a' from pushover.net/apps/build, user key starting with 'u' from the dashboard) and asks the user for both before writing anything. It does not invent, guess, or proceed with placeholder credentials.
expectations: Both credentials are requested — application/API token AND user key — not just one
The 'a' vs 'u' prefix distinction is stated so the user can tell them apart
No credentials are written to disk and no send is attempted before the user supplies real values
It is stated that this complements, not replaces, the existing macOS desktop notification
No fabricated success claim — delivery is never asserted without an API response

evals.prompt: Here's my Pushover key: u46cj64eyovssko7276jpwdgijqdqv — set it up and send me a test.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes only the user key was supplied (it starts with 'u'), asks for the application token as well, and does not attempt a send with one credential. Once both are present it validates via /1/users/validate.json, writes ~/.claude/pushover.env at mode 600, sends a test through scripts/notify-pushover.sh with PUSHOVER_DEBUG=1, and reports the raw API response.
expectations: Identifies the supplied value as the user key (u-prefix) and requests the missing application token
Does not call /1/messages.json with only one credential
Credentials are written to ~/.claude/pushover.env with mode 600, never inside the plugin cache directory
The test send goes through scripts/notify-pushover.sh rather than a hand-rolled curl
The raw {"status":1,...} response is shown as evidence of delivery
The user is told hooks load at session start, so the wiring applies to the next session

evals.prompt: My phone notifications from Claude Code just stopped working after I updated the plugin. Nothing arrives and there's no error.
evals.expected_output: The skill diagnoses using the troubleshooting table: checks that ~/.claude/pushover.env still exists and holds both values, confirms the settings.json hook uses the version-resolving glob rather than a hardcoded version path (the likely cause after an update), and re-runs a test with PUSHOVER_DEBUG=1 to surface the API response instead of silence.
expectations: Identifies a hardcoded version path in settings.json as the probable cause of breakage after a plugin update
Uses PUSHOVER_DEBUG=1 to convert the silent failure into a visible API response
Explains that the script exits 0 silently when unconfigured, which is why there is no error
Proposes re-running the installer to restore the glob-resolving hook command

evals.prompt: Set up phone notifications for me. I'm using Cursor.
evals.expected_output: Should check the `hooks` capability for cursor, report that push notifications rely on Claude Code's Notification hook event which Cursor does not provide, and STOP. Must not write ~/.claude/pushover.env, must not edit any settings file, and must not partially configure a hook that will never fire — a half-configured notifier is worse than none.

evals.prompt: Do I have to buy Pushover to use this plugin?
evals.expected_output: Should say no: Pushover is optional even on Claude Code. Declining it keeps the desktop banner and loses nothing else. Must not present the paid third-party service as required, and should note it is a one-time purchase after a 30-day trial rather than a subscription.

evals.prompt: Set up Pushover — my harness has no AskUserQuestion tool.
evals.expected_output: Should collect both credentials in plain prose with numbered options and proceed identically. AskUserQuestion is an enhancement, not a prerequisite; the skill must not stall or claim it cannot continue.

evals.prompt: Set up phone notifications — I'm on OpenCode.
evals.expected_output: Should find hooks unsupported for opencode in the capability registry and stop before writing anything. Must not create ~/.claude/pushover.env or edit a settings file: a half-configured notifier is worse than none, because the user believes they are covered and stops watching the terminal.
